# Starlark reader fixtures

Inputs for the unit tests of `socket_patch_core::bazel::starlark`
(`crates/socket-patch-core/src/bazel/starlark/mod.rs`). Nothing here was written by
socket-patch, and nothing here is built: no file has the name of a Bazel boundary file
(`MODULE.bazel`, `WORKSPACE`, `WORKSPACE.bazel`, `REPO.bazel`), so the directory is not a
Bazel workspace.

`.gitattributes` marks the directory `-text`. Line endings, a byte-order mark, a NUL and
bytes that are not UTF-8 are what several of these files test, and a conversion on checkout
would change them. `SHA256SUMS` lists every input here (`shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS`): every
file but itself and the `*.golden` files, which are what the reader produces. The test
`the_fixture_inputs_are_the_bytes_that_were_committed` compares each file with its line, so
a changed or added input needs its line there.

`s5/` and `s1c/` come from the probe group `starlark-include` of the Bazel-support campaign:
2026-11-11, one macOS arm64 machine (Darwin 27.0.0), bazelisk 1.30.0; nothing ran on Linux or
Windows. The group's drivers, per-cell logs and report (`starlark-include/RESULTS.md`) are in
the campaign's probe directory, outside this repository. `reduce.py <campaign probes
directory> .` is how the two directories and `SHA256SUMS` were made: run again on the
campaign's files it rewrites them byte for byte.

## `corpus/`: real files and the model they read to

Each file is a byte-for-byte copy of a file in a public repository at the tag given below
(for the Bazel Central Registry, at the commit given). `<name>.golden` beside it is the
statement model the reader produces, one statement per line with its line number; the test
`the_corpus_of_real_files_reads_to_its_goldens` compares them. After an intended change to
the reader, regenerate with

    SOCKET_PATCH_BLESS_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p socket-patch-core --lib bazel::starlark

and review the diff. The file name decides the dialect: `*MODULE.bazel` is a module file,
`*.WORKSPACE` a WORKSPACE file and `*.bzl` a macro file.

| File | Source | Why it is here |
|---|---|---|
| `bazelbuild-bazel-9.3.2.MODULE.bazel` | bazelbuild/bazel `9.3.2`: `MODULE.bazel` | a large root module: `repo_name = None`, long `maven.install` lists, tags generated by a comprehension |

Each file keeps the licence of its repository (Apache-2.0 for all of the above).

A real file that a test of the Bazel readers needs goes here, also when only one ruleset
recognizer reads it; the tests of `bazel/rulesets/*.rs` read theirs from this directory by
name. A copy inside a Rust string has no checksum and no row above, and a checkout may
convert its line endings. To add a file:

1. Copy its bytes to `corpus/<repository>-<tag>-<what>` with the ending that gives its
   dialect, and add its row above.
2. Write its golden with the command above.
3. Add its line to `SHA256SUMS` and renew the line of this README, which the new row
   changed (`reduce.py` rewrites the whole list).
4. Raise the counts the tests hold: the corpus size, the dialect counts and the number of
   listed inputs in `starlark/mod.rs`. The models of `bazel/module_file.rs` and
   `bazel/workspace_file.rs` read every `*.MODULE.bazel` and every `*.WORKSPACE` here as
   well: `real_module_files_read` and `real_workspace_files_read` hold a count each, and
   a row per file in `../models/corpus-modules.golden` and
   `../models/corpus-workspaces.golden` (`../models/README.md` says how to regenerate
   them).

## `s5/`: what Bazel accepts

Probe S5 of the Bazel-support campaign ran 60 variants of one statement
(`V = <expr>` followed by `print("S5VAL", repr(V), len(V))`) through Bazel 5.4.1, 6.6.0,
7.7.2, 8.8.2, 9.3.2 and 10.0.0rc3, as a root `MODULE.bazel`, an included segment, a `.bzl`
file, a `BUILD` file and a `WORKSPACE`; 2026-11-11, one macOS arm64 machine. The driver, the
per-cell logs and the full table are in the campaign's probe directory
(`starlark-include/RESULTS.md` section 2.4), outside this repository.

- `module/<variant>`, `workspace/<variant>`: the byte-exact files the probe fed to Bazel.
- `bare/<variant>`: the vectors of the segment, `.bzl` and `BUILD` kinds, which are the same
  bytes (no `module()` or `workspace()` header). `tab-indent-def-body` exists for `.bzl` only.
- `accepts.tsv`: what Bazel did, one row per kind and variant: for each distinct outcome
  the versions that had it, then the printed `repr(V) len(V)` or `error`. Derived from the
  probe's `s5/accepts-<kind>-<version>.json`.
- `verdicts.golden`: what the reader does with each vector: `value "<text>" <len>`,
  `opaque` (the file is read and `V` has no value) or `refuse <kind>`.

The test `s5_verdicts_agree_with_what_bazel_accepts` holds the two together: a value must
be the one every Bazel printed, a refusal needs every Bazel to have rejected the file, and
everything else must be opaque.

## `s1c/`: `include()` in a root `MODULE.bazel`

Probe S1c ran 35 root-module layouts through `bazel mod graph` on Bazel 6.6.0, 7.1.2, 7.2.0,
7.7.2, 8.0.0, 8.1.0, 8.8.2, 9.3.2 and 10.0.0rc3 (`RESULTS.md` section "S1c include syntax and
placement"). Here are the 27 whose root `MODULE.bazel` is the thing varied: how the label is
spelled, how the statement is written, `dev_dependency`, and where the statement stands. The
other eight vary the included segment, nest includes or use a non-root module; their root file
is the baseline's.

- `rows/<row>`: the byte-exact root `MODULE.bazel` the probe wrote for the row. The file is
  named after the probe's row, except `label-at-main`, `label-atat-main` and `label-at-s1`,
  which are its rows `label-@//`, `label-@@//` and `label-@s1//`. In every row the segment
  `.socket/bazel/socket-patch.MODULE.bazel` declares one `bazel_dep`, and the row is `ok` when
  that module shows in the graph. `dev_dependency-True+ignore_dev` is the file of
  `dev_dependency-True` run with `--ignore_dev_dependency`.
- `accepts.tsv`: what Bazel did, one row per file: for each distinct outcome the versions
  that had it. `ok` is exit 0 with the segment evaluated, `skipped` exit 0 without it, `error`
  any other exit. 6.6.0 and 7.1.2 have no `include` and reject every row. Derived from the
  probe's `s1/syntax-<version>.json`.
- `verdicts.golden`: what the reader makes of the `include` statements of each file:
  `include "<label>" dev=<bool>` for one that is read in full, `inexact` for one whose label
  or keywords are not, `not a statement` for a call of `include` that is no statement of its
  own, or `refuse <kind>`.

The test `s1c_include_rows_agree_with_what_bazel_accepts` holds the two together: in a file
some Bazel evaluated, every include is read in full, and only 9.3.2 and 10.0.0rc3 take
`dev_dependency`. Bazel also rejects rows the statement reader reads in full (a label that
starts with `@`, a file name that does not end in `.MODULE.bazel`): those are the label
reader's to refuse.
